title: Gradient budget lifecycle — headcount & pricing sensitivity sandbox
content:
Purpose and framing:
This is a compact modeling sheet intended to test a "gradient" approach to budget phasing: rather than binary hire/no-hire steps, we model continuous headcount ramp and incremental price adjustments and measure their combined impact on runway and unit margin. Use this when evaluating mid-sprint price nudges, one-off promotional credits, or phased hiring windows.

Top-level assumptions (apply uniformly unless noted):
- Baseline cash on hand: $48.2M
- Monthly burn (excluding new hires): $3.6M
- Baseline headcount (core): 142 FTEs (engineering + product + ops + go-to-market)
- Average fully-burdened cost / FTE (current): $16.2k / month
- Token unit economics baseline: contribution margin per 1k tokens = $0.004 (post-GPU and infra)
- Expected organic revenue growth w/o price changes: 4.5% / month (conservative)
- Price sensitivity elasticities tested: -5%, 0%, +5% relative to current price (three buckets)
- Hiring delay sensitivity: on-time (0 weeks), slow (+6 weeks), paused (+12 weeks)
- Quantization/efficiency uplift options considered: none / modest (5%) / aggressive (12%)

Model grid (scenarios):
We run 18 combined scenario permutations (3 price deltas x 3 hiring delays x 2 efficiency bands). For readability below we summarize representative outputs. Full simulation workbook lives in the linked GH PR.

Representative scenarios summary (monthly):
Columns: scenario_id | price_delta | hire_delay | efficiency_uplift | net_monthly_burn | runway_months | comments
S1 | -5% | 0w | 0% | $3.92M | 12.3 | Price cut increases usage but worsens short-term runway
S2 | 0% | 0w | 0% | $3.60M | 13.4 | Baseline
S3 | +5% | 0w | 0% | $3.28M | 14.7 | Price rise improves runway but risks demand drop (not modeled here)
S4 | -5% | +6w | 5% | $3.65M | 13.2 | Buffer from efficiency offsets part of price cut impact
S5 | 0% | +12w | 12% | $3.10M | 15.8 | Hiring pause + aggressive efficiency materially extends runway
S6 | +5% | +12w | 0% | $2.96M | 16.2 | Delayed hires + price increase maximizes short-term runway

Key levers and non-linearities observed in runs:
- Hiring cadence has a near-linear effect on immediate burn but creates step risks when hires arrive (lumpy costs). Gradual hiring ramps (2–4 FTE / month) smooth this risk and were modelled explicitly in the workbook.
- Small price increases (+3–7%) produce outsized short-term margin improvements if demand remains inelastic; however downstream churn risks could appear after 6–8 months — tag any +price experiment with an eval cohort and NPS/usage guardrail.
- Efficiency (quantization + batching) is multiplicative on margin and is the cheapest lever with minimal customer surface risk. Model shows 5% infra uplift buys ~0.8–1.1 months of runway depending on hire timing.

Micro-sensitivity outputs (select):
- 1% price change (up) ≈ +0.12 months runway at current scale when hires are on schedule.
- 1 week hiring delay for 6 planned hires ≈ +$97k saved that month; but when hires join, burn increases by a larger cumulative amount due to onboarding ramp + stock comp accrual.
- 1% efficiency uplift ≈ +$45k / month at current usage profile (conservative estimate).

Cash flow waterfall (illustrative quarter Q1 projection):
- Opening cash: $48.2M
- Organic revenue: $4.8M (quarter) baseline
- Price +5% sensitivity incremental: +$0.24M / quarter (modeled)
- Hiring add: +$0.9M / quarter (if hiring on schedule, 9 net new FTEs)
- Efficiency uplift (12% aggressive): -$0.55M / quarter
- Closing cash (S6-like): $51.19M (note: conservative assumptions around revenue retention)

Operational guidance for finance / product partnership:
- Any >+3% price move should require a 12-week A/B eval with matched retention/usage metrics and a rollback plan.
- Prioritize efficiency stack workstreams that deliver >5% margin uplift: request engineering roadmap alignment for batching/kv cache work and quantization pilots.
- Institute a "gradual hiring" fiscal guardrail: default ramp is 2 hires / month; deviations require finance sign-off and a scenario re-run in the workbook.

Quick checklist for next meeting (Nov planning):
- [ ] Run full 18-scenario sensitivity with updated customer cohort activation rates (Priya)
- [ ] Attach revised hiring cadence (SWE + SRE) to compensation phasing (Ethan)
- [ ] Draft price-test A/B spec and retention guardrails (Product)
- [ ] Confirm quantization pilot scope and estimate (Applied ML)

Open questions / discussion items:
1) How conservative should we be on demand elasticity after +5% price steps? Use cohort-based elasticity in next run.
2) Are there regulatory or channel constraints for raising list prices in EU customers that would change impact timing? (Legal to confirm)
3) Can we offshore any hiring windows to reduce short-term fully-burdened costs and what is the productivity delta?

Notes to self (work-in-progress):
- This sheet intentionally biases toward finance defensibility: use lower-bound revenue retention when reporting runway to the execs.
- The accompanying simulation notebook includes stochastic churn and a scenario for a mid-quarter demand shock (-18% consumption for 6 weeks). Link above.

Recommended narrative for leadership slide (one-liner):
"Adopt a gradient-phasing plan: prioritize low-friction efficiency gains and phased hiring while gating price increases with cohort-level evals — this combination extends runway by 1.5–3 months in most modeled permutations."
